newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-ELS ATTEMPTS TO RECAPTURE 1994 FORM.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELS ATTEMPTS TO RECAPTURE 1994 FORM.

text.p: Ernie Els, once dubbed "the next golfing god", believes he can recapture his brilliant 1994 form at this week's World Matchplay championship.
"I feel it's coming again. I'm playing well and my whole life is happy. There are no distractions. Everything in my life is perfect," he said.

The fair-haired giant from Johannesburg, who turns 27 on Thursday's first day of the event, is unbeaten in the Matchplay and even before his team went out of the Alfred Dunhill Cup in Sunday morning's semifinals, he was looking forward to Wentworth.

Els, who has a first round bye and who will begin his title pursuit on Friday, has sorted out a lapse in his putting which affected his game until he was helped by Greg Norman, compatriot David Frost and New Zealander Frank Nobilo during last month's President's Cup team event in Virginia.
"They told me my blade was not quite square to the ball and I was moving on the putts," he said.

He gave a hint of his rediscovered prowess on the greens of St Andrews on Sunday where, despite South Africa's semifinal loss to New Zealand, he beat Nobilo with a burst of seven birdies in eight holes in mid-round.
Els sank putts of 10, 12, 14, 13 and 12 feet in that stretch.
"When my putter gets hot, I feel I can just walk on the course and a 65 is the result," he said.
"The last two years there, I have felt comfortable with my game. I felt I could just go out there and play my shots and try to make as many birdies as I can.

"Matchplay is a little more intense than stroke play. It's also a little more mental. Sometimes you don't try to hit the ball as far as you can off the tee because you want to hit your approach in before your opponent.
"I enjoy it, and I love Wentworth. Even though it's the end of the season the course is always in great shape."

Els burst into prominence in 1992 by winning the South African Open, PGA and Masters titles, fully justifying his decision some years earlier that golf, not tennis at which he was also promising, was to be his future.
He beat a strong international field to win the prestigious Dunlop Phoenix title in Japan in 1993, his only victory that year.
In 1994, his career really took off.
Els shot a stunning 61 in the opening round of the Desert Classic in Dubai that year and went on to win by six strokes.
Then he was second in the British PGA at Wentworth and in the Buick Classic on the U.S. Tour, where he went on to win the U.S. Open title after a playoff against Loren Roberts and Colin Montgomerie.
After that, his first World Matchplay title arrived. He added the Sarazen World Open and the Johnnie Walker World Championship in Jamaica, again by six shots.
Els's triumph at Wentworth included a victory in his first match by 2 and 1 over Seve Ballesteros just a day after the Spaniard had crushed Frost 8 and 6 in the opening round.
Most golfers would be delighted to have the year Els had in 1995 though it was slightly down on his 1994 form as he struggled to adjust to full-time life on the U.S. Tour.
He won the Byron Nelson Classic and had a second, a third and a fourth as he improved his position on the money list from 19th to 14th.

This year he also occupies 14th spot with winnings of $804,944 after a victory in the Buick Classic and he was joint second in the British Open at Royal Lytham and at the Buick Open. He has missed only one halfway cut.
Yet he looks for an improvement next year and wants to add to his total of major titles, the 1994 U.S. Open being the only one in his resume so far.
"John Daly is the only player under 30 with two majors (1991 PGA, 1995 British Open) and if I play well over the next few years maybe I can win another two or three," he said.
